properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in St. Marys County.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 3 AM EDT Friday, especially
around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, water covers roads on Saint George
Island, is in yards, and is approaching structures. To the
east, inundation is occurring at multiple marinas off St.
Mary's River, Smith Creek, and Jutland Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides two to two and a half feet above
normal. The next high tide at Coltons Point is at 1:07 AM and
1:25 PM. The next high tide at Point Lookout is at 11:15 PM and
11:55 AM. The next high tide at Piney Point is at 12:31 AM and
12:49 PM.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
At 651 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marquez, Cebolletita, Seboyeta, Bibo, Paguate and Encinal.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

San Juan River in New Mexico has not been observed since before the
completion of Navajo Dam in 1962. In the Farmington vicinity,
backwater flooding on the Animas River at and above the confluence
with the San Juan River is the major concern. See flood bulletins
pertaining to the Animas River. Downriver through Shiprock, mostly
low lying and agricultural areas are subject to inundation.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:00 PM MDT Thursday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 8.9 feet just after midnight tonight. It
will then fall below flood stage early Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.2
feet on 06/29/1927.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Sandoval County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 1230 AM MDT.

* At 630 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.75 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Areas along New Mexico State Route 4 such as Jemez Springs, Jemez
State Monument, Fenton Lake State Park, Jemez Pueblo, Canon and
Ponderosa.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly or mountainous terrain there are numerous low water
crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

18 miles south of Reserve, moving northeast at 45 mph.

properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

hazardous driving conditions.

portion of west central New Mexico.
